purpose: Hand-labelled cases for checking the M15 answer judge before trusting it. Sources are real passages of the evaluation corpus; answers are written by hand, each with a known defect (or none). Labels are at answer level because claim splitting varies between calls.

labels.all_supported: every factual claim is stated by the sources (paraphrase and arithmetic allowed)
labels.citation_ok: every cited claim cites a source that states it (null: not what the case tests)
labels.correctness: acceptable verdicts against the reference answer
labels.relevance: does the answer address the question

AL3.document: NX-HR-002 v3.0 · Annual Leave and Leave Management Policy
AL3.text:
Table 4.1 – Entitlement per leave year
| Leave type | Entitlement | Credit method |
|---|---|---|
| Annual Leave | 20 working days | Accrues at 1.67 days per month, credited on the first day of each month |
| Sick Leave | 8 working days | Credited in full on 1 January |
| Casual Leave | 6 working days | Credited in full on 1 January |

Table 4.1 – Entitlement per leave year (version 2.0)

CF.document: NX-HR-002 v3.0 · Annual Leave and Leave Management Policy
CF.text:
6.1 Carry-forward
Up to 10 days of unused AL may be carried forward from one leave year to the next. AL above 10 days lapses on 31 December.
6.2 Leave that does not carry forward
SL, CL, Restricted Holidays and Compensatory Off are not carried forward and lapse on 31 December, or earlier where Section 7 says so.
6.3 No year-end encashment
Unused AL is not encashed at the end of the leave year.

EXP.text:
4.2 Submission periods
| Claim submitted | Treatment |
|---|---|
| Within 30 calendar days of the expense date (for travel, of the trip's return date) | Processed normally |
| 31 to 60 calendar days after | Processed only with Department Head approval of the delay |
| More than 60 calendar days after | Rejected |
4.4 Payment
Claims fully approved by the 20th of a month are paid with that month's salary. Claims approved after the 20th are paid with the following month's salary.

DMG.document: NX-IT-003 v1.0 · IT Asset Issuance and Return Procedure
DMG.section: 6. Damage, Loss and Theft › 6.4 Accidental damage
DMG.text: The first accidental damage repair within 24 months is free of charge. For any further accidental damage within 24 months, the employee pays 50% of the repair cost, up to a maximum of ₹15,000 per incident. Deliberate damage is charged at the full repair cost or the recovery value, whichever is lower, and may be treated as a violation under NX-GOV-002.

cases.question: How much unused annual leave can I carry forward?
cases.answer: You can carry forward up to 10 days of unused Annual Leave to the next leave year [1].
cases.expected: Up to 10 days; Annual Leave above 10 days lapses on 31 December.

cases.question: How much unused annual leave can I carry forward?
cases.answer: You can carry forward up to 10 days of unused Annual Leave [1]. Carried-forward days must be used by 31 March of the next year or they lapse [1].
cases.expected: Up to 10 days; Annual Leave above 10 days lapses on 31 December.
cases.notes: Any limit other than 10 days is wrong.

cases.question: What happens if I submit an expense claim late?
cases.answer: A claim submitted 31 to 60 calendar days after the expense is processed only if your Department Head approves the delay [1].
cases.expected: 31-60 days late: processed only with Department Head approval; more than 60 days: rejected.
cases.notes: Both bands are needed for a full answer.

cases.question: When are approved expense claims paid?
cases.answer: Claims submitted within 30 calendar days of the expense date are processed normally [1].
cases.expected: Claims fully approved by the 20th are paid with that month's salary; later approvals with the following month's.
cases.notes: The question is about payment timing.

cases.question: Can I encash my unused annual leave at the end of the year?
cases.answer: No. Unused Annual Leave is not encashed at the end of the leave year [1]. Under Indian labour law, leave encashment is only mandatory on retirement.
cases.expected: No: unused Annual Leave is not encashed at year end.

cases.question: I will have 14 days of unused annual leave on 31 December. How many will lapse?
cases.answer: 4 days will lapse: you can carry forward up to 10 days, and Annual Leave above 10 days lapses on 31 December [1].

cases.question: When are approved expense claims paid?
cases.answer: If your claim is fully approved by the 20th of the month, it is paid with that month's salary; if it is approved later, with the next month's salary [1].
cases.expected: Claims fully approved by the 20th are paid with that month's salary; later approvals with the following month's.
cases.notes: The question is about payment timing.
